purpose: Vetted transcription of NAPIC official commercial property indicators SPECIFIC TO KUALA LUMPUR sub-district / precinct level, and KL-only historical overhang and supply-pipeline series, for use on myproperty.investmquest.com. Companion file to data/napic-commercial.json (state-level national comparison, produced by a separate concurrent session) — this file goes one level deeper, into KL's own internal precinct breakdown. Produced 2026-08-12 by transcribing already-downloaded NAPIC quarterly Excel tables; no new downloads were made. Promoted to v1 on 2026-08-12 after human spot-check of sub-district cells and new history values against the source XLS.
discipline: Every value is transcribed directly from a cell in one of the official NAPIC quarterly Excel tables listed in rawFilesUsed below (already downloaded to disk for a companion transcription task). Nothing is interpolated, estimated, smoothed, or sourced from any second-hand republication. Missing/not-disclosed by NAPIC ('ND'/'NA' in source cells, meaning the precinct has no stock in that category) = null. Every value carries a source.file/sheet/row citation. No derived values appear in this file except where explicitly flagged with a 'basis' field.

notes.tableStructureTable8: Table 8 lays each state out as: a state-name header row, then one 3-row block per price band (row1=Unit Launched, row2=Unsold Units, row3=Value RM Million), ending in a 'TOTAL' 3-row block (same row1/row2/row3 pattern, with 'TOTAL' printed in the Price Range column of row1). The value this file reports as *_unsold_units / *_unsold_value_rm_million is always the TOTAL block's row2/row3 — i.e. the state's aggregate unsold-completed ('overhang') count and RM value across all price bands, matching the same convention used in the companion data/napic-commercial.json file. Column layout (0-indexed): col11 = SHOP Total, col13 = SOHO, col14 = Serviced Apartment.
notes.shoppingComplexVsCentre: Table 2.1 ('Kompleks Perniagaan'/Shopping Complex, 3,386.19 '000 sm existing, 115 buildings) and Table 3.1 ('Pusat Beli-Belah'/Shopping Centre, 2,998.84 '000 sm existing, 83 buildings) are two distinct NAPIC series for W.P. Kuala Lumpur, not one a subset relabelling of the other — see data/napic-commercial.json notes.shoppingComplexVsCentre for the same distinction at national level. Both are reported here in full since they share the same 24 precinct names, letting the two be compared precinct-by-precinct if useful; Shopping Centre is consistently the narrower of the two (fewer/smaller buildings in several precincts, e.g. Bukit Bintang/Jalan Raja Chulan 570.52 vs 502.81 '000sm, Pudu Area 192.47 vs 139.72 '000sm), consistent with it being a stricter/narrower classification.
notes.buildingCountCrossCheck: For every one of the 3 sub-district tables (PBO, Shopping Complex, Shopping Centre), the sum of total_buildings across all listed precincts was verified to equal the state TOTAL row's total_buildings exactly (PBO: 306+113=419; Shopping Complex: sum of 24 precincts=115; Shopping Centre: sum of 24 precincts=83), and the sum of total_existing_space_000sm across precincts matches the state total to within rounding (<=0.01 '000sm on 3,000-9,600 '000sm bases). This confirms the precinct lists are complete (no precinct rows were skipped).
notes.ndPrecincts: 5 precincts (Stadium Area, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Jalan Klang Lama, Jalan Pahang, Jalan Sentul) show zero existing space in both Shopping Complex and Shopping Centre tables for Q1 2026, with occupancy_rate_pct/availability_rate_pct recorded by NAPIC as 'ND'/'NA' respectively (transcribed here as null) — i.e. these precincts currently have no shopping complex/centre stock recorded, not a data-quality gap.
notes.pboPrecinctGranularity: Unlike the retail tables' 24-precinct breakdown, the PBO (Purpose-Built Office) sub-district table for W.P. Kuala Lumpur (Table 1.1) only splits into 2 precincts: 'City Centre (Seksyen 1-100, Bandar KL)' and 'Outside City Centre (Luar Seksyen 1-100, Bandar KL)'. This is the full granularity NAPIC publishes for KL office space — not a truncation on this file's part.
notes.stockPipelineSubAreas: The Jadual Stok Harta Perdagangan TABLE 2 sub-area names (Bandar Kuala Lumpur, Bandar Petaling Jaya, Mukim Ampang, Mukim Batu, Mukim Cheras, Mukim Hulu Kelang, Mukim Kuala Lumpur, Mukim Petaling, Mukim Setapak) are NAPIC's own mukim/administrative-area classification for tracking supply pipeline, and are NOT the same set of names as the CBSA occupancy tables' 24 commercial precincts (e.g. 'Bangsar', 'Bukit Bintang'). The two classification schemes should not be merged or cross-mapped without further verification; they are kept as separate datasets in this file (subdistricts vs pipeline.subdistricts).

annual_report_2025_kl_private_office_occ.scope: Privately-owned Purpose-Built Office buildings only ('bangunan pejabat milik persendirian' / 'privately owned office buildings') — distinct in period (annual FY2025 vs this file's Q1 2026 quarterly reading) but same private-only scope as pbo_purpose_built_office.kl_total above.
annual_report_2025_kl_private_office_occ.translationDiscrepancyNote: The source PDF's Malay and English text disagree on which SECOND state is named alongside WP Kuala Lumpur as below the national average (Malay: 'WP Kuala Lumpur dan Johor... masing-masing pada 70.9% dan 71.8%'; English: 'WP Kuala Lumpur and Selangor recorded lower occupancy rates... at 70.9% and 71.8%, respectively') — an inconsistency in NAPIC's own source document. Both language versions agree WP Kuala Lumpur is listed first and paired with 70.9%, so only that figure (KL, 70.9%) is used in this file; the second state's identity and its 71.8% figure are NOT used anywhere on this site because the source itself is ambiguous on which state it belongs to.
annual_report_2025_kl_private_office_occ.usageCaveat: This annual, private-only 70.9% is a DIFFERENT NAPIC scope/period from the private+government 72.6% figure already in the companion national file (data/napic-commercial.json) — never plot or compare these two on the same line/series. It is closest in scope to this file's own pbo_purpose_built_office.kl_total.occupancy_rate_pct (71.87%, Q1 2026, private-only): the two differ by <1pp across different periods, consistent with a KL office market holding in the 70-72% band rather than moving sharply.
